logLevelRemap.description: Demote the timestamp-optional notice from WARN to INFO. Mend renders every WARN in a red 'Repository problems' banner on the dependency dashboard, and this one fires on every run for any repo using a registry that does not publish release timestamps (public.ecr.aws, private ECR, GHCR, Quay) -- which is most of ours. It reports expected behaviour, not a failure: the update was raised rather than frozen. Left at WARN it is a permanent false alarm that trains engineers to ignore the banner.
logLevelRemap.matchMessage: /Some .+ did not have a releaseTimestamp, but as we're running with minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour=timestamp-optional, proceeding/

logLevelRemap.description: Demote the npm --before fallback notice from WARN to INFO, for the same banner reason. Setting minimumReleaseAge makes Renovate pass --before to npm during lock file generation; every lockfile we already have contains packages published inside the last 7 days, so npm returns ETARGET and Renovate retries without the flag. That is handled and non-fatal -- the lockfile is still written -- and it self-heals once lockFileMaintenance regenerates the file. Without this, every npm repo shows a red banner for the first week. The same text is also pushed to artifactNotices, so it still appears in the PR body where it is actually actionable.
logLevelRemap.matchMessage: /npm `--before` could not be enforced because existing locked packages were published after the/

packageRules.description: Keep internal GitHub Actions and reusable workflows on their branch or version tags so they receive updates without SHA pinning.
Keep the Knock React adapter and its client together so adapter updates do not leave incompatible client versions installed.
Update every @orpc/* package together, to the same version: ORPCError's instanceof check fails across oRPC versions, so a mismatched @orpc/nest turns oRPC 4xx errors into 500s.
Keep NestJS below v12 while services use @ts-rest/nest, which supports NestJS 11 at most. Lift the hold once services have replaced ts-rest with oRPC.
Hold direct zod bumps below v4 until ts-rest is migrated off across repos. Multiple zod majors in one dependency tree do not work together and have broken frontend consumers before.

Bump every Node and npm pin in a repository in one PR: mise.toml, .nvmrc, .node-version, .tool-versions, engines, packageManager, actions/setup-node and official Node images. Separate PRs would let the runtime in CI, Docker and local tooling drift apart, and leave npm in mise.toml disagreeing with engines.npm. Patches and minors each get their own grouped PR, because Renovate applies the first update's schedule and release age to the whole branch: patches take the fast path below, and minors follow the normal schedule and automerge. internalChecksFilter none makes every pin take the newest release and keeps pins that have not reached their release age in the branch, where they hold its stability check and automerge, instead of dropping them. Under the default strict filter, the ECR mirror, which has no release timestamps, would take a release that the timestamped pins are still waiting on, so its Dockerfile could merge alone or on a different version. Renovate reads this setting before it classifies the update type, so it cannot be limited to patches. Minors still wait their 7 days, but through the status check rather than by delaying the branch.

Keep @types/node out of the Node.js group and disabled. Renovate takes a grouped branch's schedule and release age from its first update, so a @types/node bump in the group would put Node patches back on the 7-day, weekday path.

Move engines.npm ranges with the exact npm pin. Under the preset's replace strategy a patch such as 11.19.2 still satisfies ~11.19.0, so only mise.toml and packageManager would change and the pins would read differently. Bumping keeps engines.npm on the same version as the exact pins.

Do not open major updates. A major can change APIs and needs a planned migration, so it is raised by the owning team when they choose to take it, not by Renovate. Vulnerability fixes that need a major still open, because vulnerabilityAlerts forces them on; automerge stays off so a person reviews them.

Re-assert 7 days for npm. config:best-practices pulls in security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm, whose packageRule pins npm to 3 days; preset rules resolve before ours and override the top-level minimumReleaseAge, so npm needs this to reach 7 days.

Do not require Minimum Release Age for update types Renovate cannot age. Renovate does not wire a release timestamp into these, so under the default minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour=timestamp-required they would otherwise be held back indefinitely.
prBodyNotes: ⚠️ Renovate cannot enforce Minimum Release Age for this update type, so this PR was raised without the usual 7-day check. Validate the release age manually before merging.

packageRules.description: Do not require Minimum Release Age for pinDigest updates only. A pinDigest ages against the newest version matching the current value, so a fast-releasing reference may never clear a 7-day check -- leaving it perpetually unpinned, which is less safe than pinning to a slightly-stale release. Plain `digest` updates are deliberately NOT exempted: Docker Hub ages them against `tag_last_pushed`, so a malicious re-push restarts the delay, and exempting them would hand that straight to the digest automerge rule. Registries without timestamps (GHCR, Quay, ECR) and unversioned refs are already handled by minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour=timestamp-optional, which raises them with a warning rather than holding them.
prBodyNotes: ⚠️ pinDigest updates are not age-checked. Initial SHA pins of version-tagged actions/* GitHub Actions may automerge after checks; validate release age manually for other pinDigest updates.

packageRules.description: Pin official GitHub Actions to immutable SHAs while retaining their existing version tags. Passing checks gate automerge.
The cbh-core sync workflow updates this package and regenerates the synced rules, which Renovate cannot do.
Terraform provider, module, and runtime updates need compatibility assessment and plans against existing state before merging.
Terraform CLI versions need compatibility assessment, including version files and tool-version managers.
prBodyNotes: Validate Terraform CLI compatibility by running the affected plans against existing state, including plan JSON generation. Skipped plans do not establish compatibility.

packageRules.description: Include existing-state plan guidance on Terraform and Terragrunt updates, including lockfile maintenance.
prBodyNotes: Validate the resolved versions and migration requirements, then run the affected Terraform plans against existing state, including plan JSON generation. Skipped plans do not establish compatibility.

packageRules.description: Ship Node and npm patch releases as soon as CI is green. Node security fixes ship as patch releases, so waiting 7 days and for the weekday schedule would leave known vulnerabilities in production. Patches carry no API changes, which is what makes the shorter age acceptable. One day, not zero, gives the official images time to publish the matching tag, so the group bumps the Dockerfile with the other pins. The Node.js group rule holds the branch until every pin reaches this age. A high prPriority lets them go ahead of other branches waiting on the concurrency limits.

Give the one-time digest pin of Node images its own branch. In the Node.js group it would share the minor branch, turn off that branch's automerge until someone merged the pin, and lend the branch its unaged release age.
